title: A flaw was found in nfs-utils. The fsidd daemon improperly handles input received over its local domain socket by relying on program assertions to… (CVE-2026-89098)
description: A vulnerability in nfs-utils' fsidd daemon allows a local user to cause a denial of service by sending malformed input over the local domain socket. The daemon relies on program assertions to verify command arguments, and a malformed request lacking required arguments triggers an assertion failure, crashing the daemon and disrupting filesystem identifier lookup services until restarted.
aiSummary: The fsidd daemon in nfs-utils improperly handles input received over its local domain socket by relying on program assertions to validate command arguments. A local attacker can exploit this by sending a malformed request missing required arguments, causing an assertion failure that crashes the daemon. This results in a denial of service affecting filesystem identifier lookup services until the daemon is manually restarted.
aiImpact: The vulnerability leads to a denial of service condition by crashing the fsidd daemon, which disrupts filesystem identifier lookup services. There is no impact on confidentiality or integrity, only availability is affected.
